title: Beyond the 956: Tinto Brass, Italian director of 'Caligula,' dies at 93
excerpt: Italian film director Tinto Brass has died at 93. His family announced on November 4, 2026, that he died that morning in Rome; no cause of death was disclosed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Italian film director Tinto Brass has died at 93.

Brass died on the morning of Wednesday, November 4, 2026, in Rome. His wife, Caterina Varzi, and his children, Bonifacio and Beatrice Brass, announced his death to the Italian press, and the family asked for a strictly private funeral. No cause of death was disclosed.

Born Giovanni Brass in Milan on March 26, 1933, he began his film career in avant-garde cinema, working at the Cinémathèque Française and as an assistant to director Roberto Rossellini before making his directorial debut in 1963.

He became internationally known for the controversial historical epic Caligula (1979), starring Malcolm McDowell, Peter O'Toole and Helen Mirren, from a screenplay by Gore Vidal. Brass later objected to changes made to the film during production and editing, and the finished version became one of the most notorious productions in film history.

His earlier international breakthrough, Salon Kitty (1976), and later films including The Key (La chiave, 1983) made him one of the most recognizable figures in European cinema of his era. His health declined after a cerebral hemorrhage in 2010, and in September 2026 the Venice Film Festival screened a restored version of his early film Col cuore in gola as a tribute he was unable to attend for health reasons.

Rest in Peace, Tinto Brass.

Sources: Euronews; The A.V. Club, reporting IndieWire and the family's announcement to the Italian press; Sky TG24.
